story: Eielson Air Force Base, one base and two federal processes: a microreactor site comment window closing September 30th, and Air Force AI data center land leases that took developer proposals in June

claims.claim: The Air Force is asking for public input on a plan to begin work in an area of Eielson Air Force Base where a small nuclear reactor would be located.
claims.verbatim: The Air Force is asking for public input on a plan to begin work in an area on Eielson Air Force Base where a small nuclear reactor would be located.
claims.notes: Lead paragraph. In window. The primary notice page https://www.eielson.af.mil/microreactor/ returned HTTP 403 today. The Wayback route (web.archive.org) is blocked for this fetcher, and a DVIDS search for Eielson microreactor returned no results. The primary notice was unreachable, so every comment-window claim rests on KUAC.

claims.claim: Public comments on the Eielson microreactor site must reach the Eielson Public Affairs Office no later than September 30th.
claims.verbatim: Members of the public can offer comments, but they must be submitted to the Eielson Public Affairs Office no later than Sept. 30.
claims.notes: Only one source. The eielson.af.mil primary returned 403. KUAC is the Fairbanks public broadcaster reporting the Air Force's own notice, and the address block in C03 and C04 is printed as the Air Force gives it. The run date is 2026-09-28, so the window closes within days.

claims.claim: Comments can be emailed to 354fw.pa.publicaffairs@us.af.mil.
claims.verbatim: Email: 354fw.pa.publicaffairs@us.af.mil
claims.notes: Printed on the page as an italic list item. The on-page mailto link confirms the address.

claims.claim: Comments can be mailed to 354 Broadway St., Suite 15A, Eielson AFB, AK 99702-2299.
claims.verbatim: Mail: 354 Broadway St., Suite 15A, Eielson AFB, AK 99702-2299
claims.notes: Printed on the page as an italic list item.

claims.claim: The Air Force's preferred microreactor site is near wetlands, so federal law requires the agency to ask for public comment first.
claims.verbatim: The Air Force's preferred site is located near wetlands, so the agency must first ask for public comment on the project, as required by federal law.
claims.notes: KUAC does not name the statute. A local official quoted in the piece mentions the Clean Water Act as a guess ('I'm sure they're following the Clean Water Act'). Do not name a statute on a slide.

claims.claim: The site is near Spruce Lake, east of the south end of the Eielson main runway, according to Air Force officials.
claims.verbatim: the work included delineating wetlands around the site near Spruce Lake, located east of the south end of the main runway.
claims.notes: This comes from an Air Force emailed response to KUAC.

claims.claim: Air Force officials say preconstruction work would include vegetation clearing, soil excavation, and filling and grading to level the site.
claims.value: vegetation clearing, soil excavation, and filling and grading
claims.verbatim: Air Force officials say preconstruction work will include site-preparation work like vegetation clearing, soil excavation, and filling and grading to prepare a level site for future construction.

claims.claim: Air Force officials said site data gathering for the draft Environmental Assessment, including wetland delineation, was completed in July.
claims.verbatim: Agency officials said that that work was completed in July.
claims.notes: The previous sentence on the page ties 'that work' to data gathering for the draft EA under NEPA.

claims.claim: According to KUAC, the Air Force expects the draft Environmental Assessment to be available to the public late next year.
claims.verbatim: That data will be used as part of the process of developing the draft Environmental Assessment that'll be available to the public late next year.
claims.notes: This is a projection. The article is dated September 20th, 2026, so 'late next year' reads as late 2027. That CONTRADICTS the scout merge, which said 'later in 2026'. Use 'expected late next year, according to KUAC' and do not convert it to a year on a slide.

claims.claim: Air Force officials anticipate the microreactor project will not require a full Environmental Impact Statement.
claims.verbatim: Air Force officials anticipate the project won't require a full-blown Environmental Impact Statement, which would take more time to complete.
claims.notes: This is an expectation, and it depends on regulators agreeing. Use 'anticipate' or 'expect'.

claims.claim: If only a draft Environmental Assessment is needed, Air Force officials hope to have the microreactor built and operational in 2030.
claims.verbatim: If federal regulators agree that only a draft Environmental Assessment is needed, Air Force officials hope to get the microreactor built and operational in 2030.
claims.notes: This is a conditional hope. Keep 'hope' and the condition. It is broadly consistent with C27, where a DAF official said in 2025 she hoped for completion 'before 2030'. The same 2025 Air and Space Forces piece said the project was running 18 months late, but that line came from a summary and was not verbatim-confirmed.

claims.claim: The Eielson microreactor would be rated at 5 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: the base would be the first U.S. military installation to be powered, at least partly, by a 5-megawatt microreactor
claims.notes: Two outlets corroborate it. Air and Space Forces (2025-06-12) says 'a 5-megawatt microreactor at Eielson Air Force Base'. World Nuclear News (2025-06-13) says 'meet a baseload electricity demand of 5 MWe'. Say '5 megawatts', not 'up to 5'. No fetched page says 'up to'.

claims.claim: Eielson would be the first U.S. military installation powered at least partly by a microreactor if the project proceeds as planned.
claims.verbatim: But if all goes according to plan, the base would be the first U.S. military installation to be powered, at least partly, by a 5-megawatt microreactor.
claims.notes: This is a conditional 'first'. Keep 'would be' and 'if all goes according to plan'. Air and Space Forces (2025) calls it 'The military's first commercial microreactor'.

claims.claim: KUAC reports the microreactor would provide backup electricity and heat for Eielson.
claims.verbatim: The so-called microreactor would provide backup electricity and heat for the base.
claims.notes: Other sources describe the role differently. KUAC says 'backup'. World Nuclear News says 'baseload electricity demand of 5 MWe'. Air and Space Forces says it would 'supplement' the coal plant. Attribute 'backup' to KUAC, or use the neutral 'electricity and heat', which Oklo's own release also uses.

claims.claim: KUAC reports that a 20 megawatt coal-fired heat and power plant has supplied Eielson since the 1950s.
claims.verbatim: Ever since the 1950s, a 20-megawatt coal-fired heat and power plant has provided energy for Eielson.
claims.notes: The size figure is DISPUTED. Air and Space Forces (C16) gives a 'max capacity of 23 megawatts'. If the coal plant is sized on a slide, attribute it ('about 20 megawatts, according to KUAC'), or use 'roughly 20 to 23 megawatts' citing both. The scout's 'replaces part of' framing is not on any page. Air and Space Forces says 'supplement'.

claims.claim: Air and Space Forces Magazine reported that the existing Eielson coal-fired plant has a maximum capacity of 23 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: The microreactor would supplement Eielson's existing coal-fired power plant, which has a max capacity of 23 megawatts.
claims.source_outlet: Air and Space Forces Magazine (David Roza)
claims.notes: Background, outside the window. It conflicts with KUAC's 20 MW (C15), so see that claim.

claims.claim: Oklo said it was issued a Notice of Intent to Award by Defense Logistics Agency Energy on behalf of the Department of the Air Force for the Eielson project.
claims.verbatim: Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO), an advanced nuclear technology company, has been issued a Notice of Intent to Award (NOITA) by the Defense Logistics Agency Energy (DLA Energy), on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (DAF)
claims.notes: Primary, the company's own statement. Its dateline reads '06.11.25 SANTA CLARA, CALIF.' Background date. Air and Space Forces corroborates: 'on June 11, when the Air Force announced it plans to award a contract for the technology to Oklo'. The af.mil release (Article 4213048) returned 403 and could not be read.

claims.claim: Under the intended award, Oklo would design, construct, own and operate the plant and supply electricity and heat to Eielson under a long-term power purchase agreement.
claims.verbatim: Oklo would design, construct, own, and operate the power plant, delivering both electricity and heat to the DAF's preferred installation, Eielson Air Force Base in Alaska, under a long-term power purchase agreement.
claims.notes: World Nuclear News carries the same wording. Air and Space Forces says 'Oklo will own the reactor while the Air Force buys the power it generates.'

claims.claim: The Air Force could award Oklo a 30 year firm fixed price contract for the Eielson power.
claims.verbatim: potentially award a 30-year, firm-fixed-price contract to Oklo after obtaining a licence from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
claims.notes: Only one source, and the primary is unreachable. The af.mil release that WNN summarizes returned 403, and Oklo's own release says only 'long-term'. The ANS article likely repeats the term but is behind a login. Keep 'could' or 'potentially'. No contract has been awarded. The scout merge gave the date as 2025-06-17, but the page is dated Friday, 13 June 2025.

claims.claim: The contract award to Oklo would come only after a license from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is obtained.
claims.verbatim: potentially award a 30-year, firm-fixed-price contract to Oklo after obtaining a licence from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
claims.notes: Air and Space Forces corroborates independently: 'The project must check off several remaining steps, including an environmental analysis, the contract negotiating and licensing process, approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and construction.'

claims.claim: Under the plan, Oklo will own the reactor while the Air Force buys the power it generates.
claims.verbatim: Oklo will own the reactor while the Air Force buys the power it generates.
claims.source_outlet: Air and Space Forces Magazine (David Roza)
claims.notes: Background. Consistent with Oklo's primary release (C18).

claims.claim: Oklo describes the Eielson project as the Department of the Air Force's microreactor pilot.
claims.verbatim: This project serves as the DAF's microreactor pilot to enhance energy resilience and reliability for critical national security infrastructure.

claims.claim: Defense Logistics Agency Energy selected Oklo, a California nuclear technology firm, for the Eielson microreactor on behalf of the Air Force.
claims.verbatim: Oklo Inc., the California-based nuclear technology firm that the Defense Logistics Agency Energy has selected for the Eielson microreactor project, on behalf of the Department of the Air Force and Department of Defense.
claims.notes: In-window confirmation that Oklo is still the selected firm. The primary is Oklo's own release (C17). KUAC's 2026 article mentions no power purchase agreement and no NRC licensing.

claims.claim: Oklo submitted a combined license application to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission for its Aurora reactor at Idaho National Laboratory on March 11th, 2020.
claims.verbatim: 03/11/20 Oklo Power Combined Operating License Application for the Aurora at INL
claims.notes: Primary NRC document index. This is the Idaho application, not an Eielson one. The page does not mention Eielson or any newer Oklo application. Oklo's release also says it 'submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.'

claims.claim: The NRC denied Oklo's Aurora combined license application for failure to supply information on January 6th, 2022.
claims.verbatim: 1/06/2022 OKLO INC. - Denial of the Aurora Combined Operating License Application for Failure to Supply Information
claims.notes: Primary. The linked document is ML21357A034. Give context if used: this was the 2020 Idaho application. The Eielson contract still depends on a future NRC license (C20). Nothing fetched shows the current status of any Eielson-specific license, so do not claim one.

claims.claim: The NRC accepted Oklo's Aurora application for review on June 5th, 2020.
claims.verbatim: Accepted for Review 06/05/20

claims.claim: In 2025 Deputy Assistant Secretary Balkus told Air and Space Forces Magazine she hoped the Eielson reactor would be complete before 2030.
claims.verbatim: Balkus told Air & Space Forces Magazine in April she hoped the reactor would be complete before 2030.
claims.source_outlet: Air and Space Forces Magazine (David Roza)
claims.notes: Background hope, not a schedule. Her title comes from the fetch summary. Only the surname was verbatim-confirmed.

claims.claim: The military has offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land in Alaska to private companies for data centers.
claims.verbatim: It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Association of Defense Communities (2026-04-28): '4,700 acres of land have been identified across Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Clear Space Force Station, and Eielson Air Force Base.' The primary DAF release could not be read. It returned 403 on af.mil (Article 4456660), on the af.mil print view and on its afrc.af.mil mirror, and the Wayback route is blocked. Google News lists that release as dated 2026-04-10. The solicitation text on the SAM mirror gives no acreage total.

claims.claim: As of mid-September no Alaska military data center projects had been awarded.
claims.verbatim: It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: In window. The HigherGov mirror of the solicitation shows no awardee, but that came from a summary rather than a verbatim line. Date this claim as of September 15th.

claims.claim: KUAC reports the Pentagon wants up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: The Pentagon wants to build up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Healy is the nearest town to Clear Space Force Station. Also see C31.

claims.claim: The Air Force invited private companies to build AI data centers at 12 locations across Alaska.
claims.verbatim: The Air Force is inviting private companies to build AI data centers in 12 different locations across Alaska
claims.notes: Background. ADC cites Aviation A2Z, not the Air Force directly. Parcel counts add up. The Eielson area has five (C40 and C41), and the JBER sites number five according to ADN on 2026-05-05 ('five sites at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson range from about 60 acres to nearly 200 acres'), which leaves two for Clear by subtraction. That split was not verified. The '12 parcels' wording in the primary could not be read. Say '12 locations, according to trade press' or 'up to a dozen' (C30).

claims.claim: The Air Force solicitation covers AI data center development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.verbatim: RFLP Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: Marked primary because the page reproduces the federal notice's own title, dates and description text. It is a third-party mirror, since SAM.gov does not render to this fetcher. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source (2026-06-08) and ADN (2026-05-05).

claims.claim: The Air Force AI data center lease solicitation is numbered AFCEC-26-R-0006.
claims.verbatim: AFCEC-26-R-0006
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: The number appears as the solicitation ID and in the page URL.

claims.claim: The AI data center lease solicitation was posted on April 10th.
claims.verbatim: April 10, 2026, 2:01 p.m. EDT (updated: June 15, 2026, 9:11 p.m. EDT )
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: Google News independently lists the DAF release 'DAF takes steps for potential Alaskan AI data centers' as dated April 10th, 2026. The notice was last updated June 15th.

claims.claim: Proposals for the AI data center leases were due June 29th at 5 p.m. Eastern.
claims.verbatim: June 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT (original: May 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT )
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: Corroborated by the News-Miner (2026-06-11), 'due by June 29', and by Alaska's News Source (2026-06-08).

claims.claim: The original proposal deadline was May 29th before it was extended to June 29th.
claims.verbatim: June 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT (original: May 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT )
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: ADN (2026-05-05) reported 'May 29 is the deadline for submissions', which matches the original date.

claims.claim: The AI data center lease solicitation was set to archive on July 14th.
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: This value is labeled Archive Date on the page.

claims.claim: The Air Force issued the data center request as a Request for Lease Proposal to lease underutilized land at fair market value under 10 U.S.C. 2667.
claims.verbatim: is supported by 10 U.S.C. § 2667, allowing the government to lease real property to non-federal entities at fair market value.
claims.source_outlet: HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov notice AFCEC-26-R-0006 (Department of the Air Force)
claims.notes: The phrase 'enhanced use lease' does NOT appear in the fetched notice text. Section 2667 is the statute behind what the military calls enhanced use leases, which is fair context but should not be presented as a quote. The notice also cites Executive Order 13327.

claims.claim: The lease solicitation identifies five potential data center spots in the Eielson area.
claims.verbatim: The RFLP identifies five potential spots in the Eielson area: one near southeast North Pole, two plots across the Richardson Highway from Eielson, one smack dab in the middle of the installation and one on the installation's north side.
claims.notes: Independently corroborated by Alaska's News Source (2026-06-08): 'Five parcels of land are referenced in the RFLP for potential development, including one near southeast North Pole, two across the Richardson Highway from Eielson, one in the heart of the Air Force base and one further north but still within Eielson.'

claims.claim: According to a resident quoted by the News-Miner, one proposed parcel is less than a mile from North Pole Middle School.
claims.verbatim: One is less than a mile from North Pole Middle School.
claims.notes: Only one source. One fetch attributed the line to resident Sarah Hollister's concerns, so it may be her claim and not the reporter's measurement. The distance was not checked against the RFLP appendices. Attribute it: 'less than a mile from North Pole Middle School, a resident told the News-Miner'.

claims.claim: The three Eielson-area parcels outside the base fence line connect to the Golden Valley Electric Association grid.
claims.verbatim: Hollister noted that the three parcels outside Eielson's fence line are connected to the Golden Valley Electric Association grid.
claims.notes: Stated by a resident. Alaska's News Source also reports that three sites would use the GVEA grid. The News-Miner says the RFLP requires lessees to get all utilities 'at its sole cost and expense', but that came from a summary.

claims.claim: A Salcha resident raised concern about data center heat affecting surrounding permafrost.
claims.verbatim: Hollister said her concern was the impact temperatures could have on the surrounding permafrost.
claims.notes: Hollister is identified as a Salcha resident in the KUAC 2026-09-15 piece. Alaska's News Source quotes her: 'data centers tend to let off a ton of heat, and what can that do to our permafrost?'

claims.claim: Salcha resident Sarah Hollister told KUAC that the 24/7 hum of a data center shows the country has lost its way.
claims.verbatim: But the sound of a 24/7 hum from a data center shows me that we have completely lost our way.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Named-person quote, verbatim on the page. It is one resident's view.

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski told KUAC she is not a proponent of data centers at JBER or Interior installations because Alaska's energy base is insecure.
claims.verbatim: I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time,
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Verbatim on the fetched page, matching the scout text exactly. The quote was published September 15th. The page does not say when she said it.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly is calling for a data center moratorium but can't direct the Pentagon on military land.
claims.verbatim: Even though the Borough Assembly is calling for a data center moratorium, it can't tell the Pentagon what to do on military land.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: This does NOT say that no public comment path exists for the leases. It supports only the limit of local authority.

claims.claim: An Air Force spokesperson said data center contractors will be required to show how they would reduce impacts and risk to surrounding communities.
claims.verbatim: Another spokesperson said the military will require data center contractors to demonstrate how they would reduce impacts and risk to surrounding communities.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: It is the Air Force side of the story, useful for balance. The same article says 'The Air Force denied multiple requests for interviews.'

claims.claim: Chugach Electric and Golden Valley Electric told ADN that with Cook Inlet gas dwindling they can't produce enough electricity for large data centers.
claims.verbatim: Electric associations that would potentially serve the facilities — Chugach Electric Association in Anchorage and Golden Valley Electric Association in Fairbanks — say that with natural gas from Cook Inlet dwindling, they can't produce enough electricity to meet the needs of large data centers.
claims.notes: Background from May. The verbatim string includes em dashes because that is how ADN printed it. Paraphrase it without dashes on any slide.

claims.claim: Executive Order 14318 counts a data center as a qualifying project when its sponsor commits at least $500 million in capital expenditures.
claims.verbatim: a Data Center Project or Covered Component Project for which the Project Sponsor has committed at least $500 million in capital expenditures as determined by the Secretary of Commerce;
claims.notes: Primary. The order is dated July 23rd, 2025 and was published in the Federal Register on July 28th, 2025. Use it for scale reference only. Nothing fetched says the Alaska leases were designated under this order.

claims.claim: Executive Order 14318 also counts a data center as a qualifying project when it adds more than 100 megawatts of new electric load.
claims.verbatim: a Data Center Project or Covered Component Project involving an incremental electric load addition of greater than 100 MW;
claims.notes: For scale, 100 MW is 20 times the 5 MW Eielson microreactor (C12) and about 4 to 5 times the 20 to 23 MW coal plant (C15, C16). That arithmetic is ours and is not stated on any page.

claims.claim: Rep. Nick Begich introduced the DATA Act of 2026 as the House companion to Senate legislation led by Sen. Tom Cotton.
claims.verbatim: introduced the DATA Act of 2026, the House companion to Senate legislation led by Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.)
claims.notes: Primary press release dated April 21st, 2026. The introduction date comes from the release date. The bill text on congress.gov was not fetched. Background for Story 2.

claims.claim: Rep. Dan Crenshaw of Texas joined Begich in introducing the House DATA Act.
claims.verbatim: Congressman Nick Begich (R-AK), along with Congressmen Dan Crenshaw (R-TX) and
claims.notes: The release names a third cosponsor from Utah, but the fetch rendered the name as 'Burgess Owels', which is probably a typo for Burgess Owens on the page or in the fetch. The spelling is unconfirmed, so that name is listed under killed.

claims.claim: Begich said the DATA Act lets manufacturers run on fully self-contained grid-of-one power systems so households don't subsidize massive new energy demand.
claims.verbatim: The DATA Act allows manufacturers to operate on fully self-contained, 'grid-of-one' power systems, so innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands or straining local utilities.
claims.notes: Verbatim sponsor quote. It is the sponsor's framing, so present it as his claim about the bill.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reports the DATA Act would let data centers run their own energy grids separate from regular utilities.
claims.verbatim: In it, he was promoting his legislation, the DATA Act of 2026, which would allow data centers to operate their own energy grids separate from regular utilities.
claims.notes: In window. The Begich release says the systems stay 'separate' from the grid ('By keeping these systems separate, the bill ensures that new industrial demand does not increase costs for existing customers or compromise grid stability.'). Neither page says the bill exempts anything from utility regulation or oversight.

claims.claim: Independent congressional candidate Bill Hill joined other independents in Washington on Thursday, September 24th, to call on Congress to return and tackle data centers.
claims.verbatim: Independent candidate Bill Hill joined other high-profile Independents in Washington, D.C., on Thursday to call for Congress to return and tackle data centers.
claims.notes: The page says only 'on Thursday'. The article is dated September 25th, 2026, a Friday, so Thursday was September 24th. That date is our derivation. Only one source.

claims.claim: Hill spoke from Capitol Hill alongside Nebraska Senate candidate Dan Osborn and North Dakota Senate candidate Brian Bengs.
claims.verbatim: Hill, a commercial fisherman, spoke to reporters from Capitol Hill, flanked by Nebraska independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn and North Dakota independent US Senate candidate Brian Bengs.

claims.claim: Hill said gasoline in his hometown costs nearly $9 a gallon.
claims.verbatim: In my hometown, gasoline is nearly $9 a gallon.
claims.notes: This is the candidate's own claim, not an independently measured price. Attribute it to Hill. The page does not name his hometown.

claims.claim: Hill said some outlying communities are going to pay $15 a gallon for heating fuel.
claims.verbatim: Some of the outlying communities are going to be paying $15 a gallon for heating fuel.
claims.notes: The candidate's projection ('going to be paying'). Attribute it to Hill.

claims.claim: If approved, the University of Alaska's draft AI policy would require all three campuses to have an AI plan for students, faculty and staff.
claims.verbatim: If approved, it would require all three campuses to have an AI plan in place for students, faculty and staff.
claims.notes: Alaska Public Media republished it on 2026-09-18 with the same content. Run No.61 (2026-09-17) already reported this draft policy, so dedupe risk is high.

claims.claim: University of Alaska leadership plans to submit a finalized AI policy draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.verbatim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.notes: A plan, not a scheduled vote. The same sentence appears on alaskapublic.org (2026-09-18).

claims.claim: UA chief information technology officer Ben Shier asked how the university ensures data privacy and protection and provides monitoring.
claims.verbatim: How do you ensure data privacy and protection? How do you provide monitoring?
claims.notes: Also on KTOO 2026-09-16, which continues 'How do you do all of those kinds of things?'

claims.claim: As of mid-September the university had not scheduled dates for student listening sessions on the AI policy.
claims.verbatim: The university plans to collect student feedback this fall through listening sessions and online surveys, but it has not scheduled any dates as of Wednesday afternoon.
claims.notes: This may be out of date by the run date. Date it as of September 16th.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Statewide AI Symposium ran September 25th to 27th at the ConocoPhillips Integrated Science Building in Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: September 25 - 27
claims.notes: The event listing has no publish date, so date_of_source is the fetch date. The same page names the venue as 'ConocoPhillips Integrated Science Building, 3101 Science Cir, Anchorage' and says a keynote by futurist Bryan Alexander closed Friday's program. We did not confirm that the event took place.

stories_surviving: Eielson, one base and two federal processes (microreactor site comment window closing September 30th and Air Force AI data center land leases)
Begich's DATA Act grid of one and Bill Hill's Capitol call for data center guardrails
University of Alaska draft system-wide AI policy headed to November regents meeting

killed.claim: A separate Eielson mixed-use lease of 3,967 acres had proposals due August 10th.
killed.why: The only cited source, eielson.af.mil Article 4550770, returned HTTP 403. afcec.af.mil also returned 403. The Wayback route is blocked, and DVIDS and Google News searches found no second source. Unverified.

killed.claim: The Air Force AI data center leases have no public comment period.
killed.why: No fetched page says this. KUAC, the News-Miner, Alaska's News Source, ADN and the solicitation mirror are all silent on a comment period. Its absence cannot be stated as fact. At most the deck can say only the microreactor site has an announced comment window, which C01 and C02 support.

killed.claim: A draft Environmental Assessment is expected later in 2026.
killed.why: Contradicted by the source. KUAC (2026-09-20) says the draft EA will be 'available to the public late next year'. C09 replaces this claim.

killed.claim: The microreactor replaces part of a 1950s coal plant.
killed.why: No fetched page says 'replace'. KUAC calls it backup, Air and Space Forces says 'supplement', and WNN says baseload. Use C14 to C16 instead.

killed.claim: The Eielson microreactor is up to 5 MW.
killed.why: No fetched page says 'up to'. All sources say 5 megawatts or 5 MWe (C12).

killed.claim: The Department of the Air Force offered 4,700 acres across 12 parcels (from the af.mil release of April 10th).
killed.why: The primary release (af.mil Article 4456660, its print view and the afrc.af.mil mirror) returned 403, and web.archive.org is blocked for the fetcher. The figures survive only as secondary claims C28 and C31, and the exact '12 parcels' wording was never seen.

killed.claim: eielson.af.mil/microreactor page contents (comment window, PPA, schedule).
